one_month_reasoning: No Meta earnings in the window (Q4 results late Jan-2027). Scheduled: Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon Q3 calls (Oct 28-30) bring the first numeric 2027 capex guides, which set the AI-spending mood that took META from $697 to $643 in two days (Oct 22 -7% after results; Oct 23 -1% with the Nasdaq -2.6%); the FTC consent-order hearing on Nov 12 [2]; NVIDIA results in mid/late November; youth-related trials 'in the coming months' and the New Mexico penalty appeal. Snap/Pinterest/Reddit Q3 prints (late Oct/early Nov) are read-across for ad pricing. No edge on direction: the stock beat on revenue and EPS but sold off on spend, so post-earnings drift and reversal pull opposite ways. Ladder is centred at ~$646 (tiny drift) with monthly vol ~12% (43%/3.5) and a 20% weight on a fatter-tailed component for capex-guide or litigation shocks.

fair_value.method: Driver-led 3-year build (impressions x price per ad for Family of Apps, FoA margin, RL loss, capex, D&A) valued at the horizon: SOTP $718 (40%), P/E 19x NTM GAAP EPS ~$35.8 = $669 (35%), EV/EBITDA 10.5x = $677 (25%); research target (12m) $691 per current pre-split share.

thesis_break_reason: Below the $520 52-week low: at $505 the market would be pricing FY2027-28 EPS ~25% under our build at 16-17x (the bear case: impressions and pricing both decelerating to low single digits, FoA margin in the low 30s) or a litigation bill well above $30B. Either means the ad engine or the legal exposure, not volatility, broke the thesis.

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP EBIT and EPS after SBC ($20,427M in FY2025, F43; $26,943M TTM, F46); share count grows +0.5% a year net (no buybacks assumed while FCF is negative); peers' P/Es are GAAP P/E on the same basis.

reasoning: Per-share figures are per CURRENT pre-split share (today's Class A share plus the Class C share it receives on 2027-01-19); EV is unchanged by the dividend. Industry lane: the rest of the ad chain says demand is still strong but slowing. WARC's Q3-26 outlook has social ad spend +21.3% in 2026 and +14.6% in 2027, total +11.9% then +8.4% [13]; IAB US social +16.5% in 2026 [14]; Google Search +17%, YouTube +13%, Amazon ads +26%, Reddit ads +64%, Pinterest +18%, Snap ads only +9% in Q2-26 [16-20]; eMarketer puts Meta's 2026 ad revenue at ~$242B [30]. Meta's own impressions growth fell from +19% (Q1) to +10% (Q3) while price per ad rose to +14% [6][5][1]; an agency newsletter reports large CPM rises [31] (lead only, low weight). On the cost side the supply chain says Meta's bill keeps rising: CoreWeave $21B through 2032 [21], Nebius $12B from early 2027 [22], DRAM contract prices still rising [23], neocloud rental pricing up >50% YTD (MS proprietary index, used only as direction) [25], $454.5B of non-cancelable commitments and $355.7B of leases not yet commenced [2]. So the driver build has FY2027 revenue +17.7% (impressions +8%, price +9%), 2.4% under consensus, and FoA margin falling to 37.4% as D&A rises to $47B; FY2027 EPS ~$31 vs $33.92 consensus. Capex follows the AI-capex file base ($141B in 2026, $192B in 2027) [24]. Guidance record: five straight quarterly revenue guides at or above the range (median +3.4% vs midpoint), expense guides inside, capex guides overshot in 2024-25. Valuation: SOTP (FoA 16x EV/EBIT, RL separately at -$94B), P/E 19x and EV/EBITDA 10.5x give a research target (12m) of $691 after -$19.9B accrued legal and -$10.5B probability-weighted litigation. Ladder: bear $455 / base $680 / bull $920 at 25/50/25 with 25% within-scenario vol (total ~35% log vol vs 43% realized); the centre (~$670 median) sits between the price and the research target because the price is the better one-year predictor. No option data used. Research limited: Q3-26 peer results (Alphabet, Snap, Pinterest, Reddit) are not out yet; X/Twitter not used; no prediction market found on a Meta event that matters (Kalshi lists only headcount contracts). In-lane sources: 19 of 31.

parts.name: Family of Apps
parts.note: NTM FoA EBIT at the horizon (0.19 x FY2027 + 0.81 x FY2028) x 16x EV/EBIT; 16x = the 19x P/E leg x (1 - 16% tax) for a near-net-cash company, i.e. the same multiple on core earnings without RL losses

parts.name: Reality Labs
parts.note: Valued on its own (playbook: never run a venture's losses through the core multiple): 60% losses narrow ~$2B a year to breakeven by ~2034 (PV of after-tax losses ~$44B); 40% losses persist at the FY2027 level and are capitalised like a cost centre at 13x after tax. -(0.6 x 44.0 + 0.4 x 15.5 x 0.84 x 13) = -$94.1B

drivers.label: Family of Apps GAAP operating margin
drivers.source: Base: FY2025 FoA operating income $102,469M / FoA revenue $198,759M = 51.55% [4]
drivers.derivation: FY2026: total opex at the $177B midpoint of the $175-179B guide [1] (includes the $9.89B Q3 legal charge, $2.4B Q2 legal charge and $1.18B severance) on $258.1B revenue = EBIT $81.1B; plus RL loss $18.5B = FoA EBIT $99.6B / $256.0B = 38.9% (44.2% ex the $13.5B of one-offs). FY2027 37.4%: opex ex one-offs grows ~26% (vs ~39% in 2026) because D&A rises ~$19B (see driver da_usd), third-party cloud contracts start (CoreWeave $21B through 2032 [21]; Nebius $12B dedicated from early 2027 [22]; $121.4B of non-cancelable commitments due in 2027 vs $45.9B for the rest of 2026 [2]) and memory/component inflation (TrendForce 4Q26 DRAM contract +10-15% QoQ [23]). drivers.why: Margin is where the AI build's cost lands; 1 pt of FoA margin in FY2028 is ~$3.4B of EBIT (~$1.1/share at 19x after tax).

model_inputs.structure_note: Driver-led set (6 drivers: ad impressions index, price-per-ad index, FoA margin, RL loss, capex, D&A; FoA = 99%+ of revenue is driven, base residual 0.0%). Value is carried by three legs on FY2027-28 figures read at the horizon: SOTP (40%: FoA at 16x NTM EV/EBIT, RL valued separately at -$94B), P/E 19x NTM on model GAAP EPS (35%), EV/EBITDA 10.5x NTM (25%). No DCF (engine rule). Adjustments: -$19.9B accrued legal liabilities (debt-like) and -$10.5B probability-weighted unaccrued youth litigation. Per-share = per current pre-split share.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) the RL valuation (-$94B, ~-$36/share in the SOTP leg) and the 40% SOTP weight; valuing RL at 0 would raise the target ~$15. (2) Net debt at the horizon is stated ($67B) rather than bridged by the engine, because Q4-26 capex (~$55B) is far above a pro-rata quarter; the bridge adds back half of SBC as cash (RSU tax withholding absorbs the rest), while EBIT bears full SBC. (3) Our FY2027 EPS (~$31) is 8.6% below the $33.92 consensus: cost growth from compute contracts and D&A; if consensus is right the target rises ~$55. Leg weights are untested judgment.
